name: The Riptide Fissure

detectability.signature: hard-edged seam of blueshifted light shedding intermittent chroniton spray along both lips

proximity: Chronometers jitter erratically, gaining and losing seconds without pattern
Crew glimpse flickering double images of their own ship slightly out of phase
contact: Vessels partially enter two timeframes at once, hull plating aged differently fore and aft
Brief sensory displacement into landscapes from distant eras
prolonged_exposure: Timeline bifurcation leaves crew members with contradictory memories of the same voyage
Individuals who never boarded appear in crew manifests and physical records

phenomena: Objects existing in multiple timeframes simultaneously
Ships appearing older or newer after passing through
Causality loops rippling into nearby star systems
opportunities: Shortcut across three hundred light-years of normal space
Recovery of lost ships and personnel displaced from other eras
known_incidents: The survey corvette Merrow's Debt vanished for eighty years, then emerged intact with her crew insisting only a single watch had passed
description: The Riptide Fissure cuts across space like a hairline crack in dark glass, a corridor of compressed light barely a thousand kilometers wide but stretching for millions. Its edges bleed a cold blue radiance, and instruments detect chroniton spray hissing from the rift like surf breaking over rocks. Background stars visible through the seam belong to seasons that have not yet occurred.

The fissure wanders without discernible pattern, opening new channels and sealing old ones in days. Ships threading the corridor emerge transformed in time rather than space, sometimes younger, sometimes carrying rust that took decades to form. Navigation computers refuse to plot courses through it twice the same way.

Charting vessels stumbled onto the rift while investigating temporal anomalies reported across three neighboring systems. The reappearance of the Merrow's Debt, eighty years after her disappearance and with all hands alive, settled every academic argument about the rift's nature. Salvage guilds now stake its shifting mouth, waiting for wreckage from other centuries to drift home.

No authority has ever held the fissure long enough to fence it, and its current channel bends toward a busy shipping lane. Researchers beg for samples its erratic drift keeps destroying, while smugglers bless the one passage no patrol dare predict. Every emergence changes the map; every map is already wrong.
